question: Who among the following Governor Generals of India formulated the Doctrine of Lapse to deal with the issue of succession in India states during colonial rule?
solution:
The correct answer is__** ​Lord Dalhousie.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The doctrine of lapse, in Indian history, a formula drawn up by** Lord Dalhousie, governor-general of India** (1848–56), to cover questions of** succession to Hindu Indian states.**
 
• It was used like an **administrative policy** for the **extension of British Paramountcy.**
 
• **Dalhousie** strongly applied the** lapse doctrine** for take over Indian princely states, but the policy was** not solely his invention. **
 
• The Court of Directors of the East India Company had hinged this **early in 1834. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Canning** proceed the** Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856** which was enlisted by his predecessor Lord Dalhousie prior to the rebellion.
 
• **Sir John Macpherson** was a British administrator in India.​ 
 
• **John Shore** scheme was to combine and **rule the colonial state well without engaging in unnecessary foreign adventures. **
